"Multiplayer (MP): Fast-paced, 5v5 competitive matches on classic Call of Duty maps (like Nuketown, Shipment, Crash, and Firing Range). It features staple modes like Team Deathmatch, Domination, Search @COMMENT_BODY@ Destroy, Hardpoint, and Kill Confirmed, alongside rotating party modes (like Prop Hunt or Gun Game).
​Battle Royale (BR): A large-scale survival mode supporting up to 100 players (solo, duo, or 4-player squads) on massive maps like Isolated and Blackout. Players parachute in, scavenge for weapons and armor, use vehicles (including helicopters and tanks), and fight to be the last team standing as the playable zone shrinks.Gunsmith: One of the game’s biggest features is its deep weapon customization. You can modify almost every part of your gun (barrels, scopes, stocks, ammunition, grips, and perks) to change how it handles, aims, and deals damage.
​Loadouts @COMMENT_BODY@ Scorestreaks: Just like the console versions, you build custom loadouts with primary/secondary weapons, tactical/lethal grenades, perks, and Operator Skills (special abilities like a flamethrower, gravity spikes, or a ballistic shield). Getting kills without dying earns Scorestreaks like UAVs, Predator Missiles, and Stealth Choppers.
​Controls: The game offers customizable touch controls (including an option where the gun fires automatically when you aim at an enemy, which is great for beginners) as well as full support for external Bluetooth controllers (like PlayStation and Xbox controllers).
​3. Progression @COMMENT_BODY@ Monetization
​Ranked Play: Both Multiplayer and Battle Royale have competitive Ranked modes where players climb tiers (from Rookie up to Legendary) to earn exclusive rewards.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
